queries: WITH c AS (SELECT p.bats AS bats, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM appearances a JOIN player p ON a.player_id = p.player_id GROUP BY p.bats) SELECT bats, cnt AS appearance_count, cnt * 1.0 / SUM(cnt) OVER () AS share_of_total, cnt * 1.0 / AVG(cnt * 1.0) OVER () AS ratio_to_avg_count FROM c

WITH c AS (SELECT p.bats AS bats, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM appearances a JOIN player p ON a.player_id = p.player_id WHERE p.bats IS NOT NULL GROUP BY p.bats) SELECT bats, cnt AS appearance_count, cnt * 1.0 / SUM(cnt) OVER () AS share_of_total, cnt * 1.0 / AVG(cnt * 1.0) OVER () AS ratio_to_avg_count FROM c

assumptions.assumption: Players with a NULL bats value form their own group (shown as NULL) and count as a batting hand group in the total and in the average per batting hand.
An appearance record is one row in the appearances table; the inner join on player_id drops rows with no matching player.

alternatives.interpretation: Exclude players whose batting hand is unknown (NULL) from the groups, the total and the average.

assumptions.assumption: Players whose bats value is NULL or blank form their own group (a NULL batting-hand group) and are included in the total and in the average count per batting hand, since the request only drops appearances with no matching player.
Each row in appearances counts as one appearance record (player-year-team rows), and the average is taken across the batting-hand groups present in the joined data.

alternatives.interpretation: Exclude players with a NULL batting hand, so only known batting hands are counted in the total and the average.
alternatives.sql: WITH c AS (SELECT p.bats AS bats, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM appearances a JOIN player p ON a.player_id = p.player_id WHERE p.bats IS NOT NULL GROUP BY p.bats) SELECT bats, cnt AS appearance_count, cnt * 1.0 / SUM(cnt) OVER () AS share_of_total, cnt * 1.0 / AVG(cnt) OVER () AS ratio_to_average_count FROM c

assumptions.assumption: Each row in appearances counts as one appearance record. An inner join to player drops rows with no matching player. If player_id were duplicated in player, the join would inflate counts. I assume it is unique.
Players with a NULL or blank bats value form their own group, shown as NULL or blank. They are not excluded. The average count per batting hand is taken over all groups returned, including that one.

alternatives.interpretation: Exclude players whose batting hand is unknown (NULL or empty). Total and average are then computed only over known batting hands.
alternatives.sql: WITH c AS (SELECT p.bats AS bats, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM appearances a JOIN player p ON a.player_id = p.player_id WHERE p.bats IS NOT NULL AND p.bats <> '' GROUP BY p.bats) SELECT bats, cnt, cnt * 1.0 / SUM(cnt) OVER () AS share_of_total, cnt * 1.0 / AVG(cnt) OVER () AS ratio_to_avg_count FROM c
